note: Rav Ḥanin related that Rav Kahana once brought a bill of divorce between Sura and Neharde'a, though he did not know in which direction. Rav Kahana asked Rav whether he had to declare: It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence. Rav said he did not have to, but that if he did, it would help. The Gemara explains: if the husband later came to contest the document, no attention would be paid to him.
why: The Gemara is discussing when an agent carrying a bill of divorce must make this declaration, and how Sages required it even for very short distances; this case gives Rav's ruling for travel between two towns in Babylonia.

note: A relative of Rabbi Asi held a promissory note with a property guarantee written in it, and asked Rabbi Asi whether the Sabbatical Year cancels it. Rabbi Asi said it does not. The man then went to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said it does. Rabbi Asi came to Rabbi Yoḥanan and pointed out that Rabbi Yoḥanan himself had said it does not, and that a baraita agreed. Rabbi Yoḥanan answered: because we think so, should we act on it? Perhaps that baraita follows Beit Shammai.
why: The Gemara has just reported that Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish hold the Sabbatical Year does not cancel a note with a property guarantee, with baraitot in support; here Rabbi Yoḥanan refuses to rule that way in practice.

people.name: Rabbi Asi
people.about: A Sage whose relative asks about a debt; he challenges Rabbi Yoḥanan

people.name: Rabbi Yoḥanan
people.about: Rabbi Asi's teacher, who rules that the debt is cancelled

terms.meaning: Every seventh year, when by Torah law outstanding debts are cancelled.
A clause in a loan document pledging the borrower's land as security for the debt.
A teaching of the early Sages that was not included in the Mishna.
The school of the early Sage Shammai, whose rulings are usually not followed in practice.

note: In Pumbedita there was a maidservant with whom people were committing forbidden sexual acts. Abaye said that were it not for Shmuel's ruling, reported by Rav Yehuda, that anyone who frees his slave violates a positive commandment, he would force her master to write her a bill of manumission. Ravina said that in a case like this, Rav Yehuda would agree she may be freed, because of the prohibition being violated.
why: The Gemara has been discussing when a master sends his maidservant a bill of manumission; after this case it asks whether Abaye truly rejects freeing a slave to stop a sin, citing a half-free woman whose master was forced to free her.

people.name: Abaye
people.about: A Sage who would force the master to free her if not for Shmuel's ruling

people.name: Ravina
people.about: A Sage who says Rav Yehuda would agree to free her here

people.name: Shmuel
people.about: The Sage who ruled that freeing one's slave violates a positive commandment

terms.meaning: A document by which a master frees a slave.
A Torah command to do something, as opposed to a prohibition.

note: Abba Sikkara, leader of Jerusalem's zealots and nephew of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, came to him in secret. Rabban Yoḥanan asked how long they would kill everyone by starvation; Abba Sikkara said the zealots would kill him if he spoke out, and told him to fake illness and death and be carried out. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua carried him, and at the gate Abba Sikkara stopped the guards from piercing or pushing him. In the Roman camp he hailed Vespasian as king, citing verses, but fell silent at Vespasian's parable of a snake around a barrel of honey. When a messenger announced Vespasian would be emperor and his shoe would not go on, Rabban Yoḥanan explained why and how to fix it.
why: The Gemara is telling the story of the siege and fall of Jerusalem; just before this, the wealthy Marta bat Baitos dies in the same famine Rabban Yoḥanan blames on the zealots.

note: Onkelos bar Kalonikos, Titus's nephew, wanted to convert. He raised Titus from the dead by necromancy and asked who matters most in that world. Titus said the Jewish people, but told him their commandments were too many to keep and he should fight them instead; asked his own punishment, Titus said his ashes are gathered, judged, burned and scattered over the seven seas every day. Onkelos raised Balaam, who told him not to seek their peace, and is punished in boiling semen. Then he raised Jesus the Nazarene, who told him to seek their welfare, and is punished in boiling excrement. The Gemara draws the contrast between the sinners of Israel and the prophets of the nations. The text here does not say what Onkelos then did.
why: The Gemara has just told of Titus's death and his order that his ashes be scattered so the God of the Jews could not judge him; here that very sentence is carried out on him every day.

people.name: Onkelos bar Kalonikos
people.about: Titus's sister's son, who wants to convert to Judaism

people.name: Titus
people.about: The Roman who destroyed the Temple, raised from the dead by Onkelos

people.name: Balaam

people.name: Jesus the Nazarene
people.about: Raised by Onkelos; the Gemara calls him a sinner of Israel who sought their welfare

terms.meaning: Calling up the spirit of a dead person to speak with them.

note: At the King's Mountain it was the custom to carry a rooster and a hen before a bride and groom. One day Roman soldiers took them, the people beat the soldiers, and the soldiers told the emperor the Jews had rebelled. He attacked. Bar Deroma, who could leap a mil, killed many Romans, until he quoted a psalm as a complaint against God; then a snake eviscerated him in an outhouse and he died. The emperor withdrew, but when the Jews celebrated with lamps, he said they were rejoicing over him and returned. Rav Asi says three hundred thousand swordsmen massacred the people for three days and nights while weddings went on at the other side, neither knowing of the other.
why: The Gemara is recounting disasters of the war with Rome; it said earlier that the King's Mountain was destroyed over a rooster and a hen, and after the story of Kamtza and bar Kamtza it now gives the details.

people.name: bar Deroma
people.about: A man of the King's Mountain who could leap a mil and killed many Romans

people.name: Rav Asi
people.about: The Sage who reports the size of the massacre

terms.meaning: Tur Malka, a large, heavily populated region of the Land of Israel.
